text:
Marathon Petroleum stock gained 0.75% today, continuing a strong two-week rally of 8%. The immediate driver appears to be falling oil prices—a Saudi pipeline damaged earlier is restarting soon, and Saudi Arabia is offering additional ship-to-ship crude transfers, both easing supply concerns that had pushed prices higher. Crude fell to $107 per barrel (down from earlier highs), which helps refiners' input costs while they continue running at nearly 97% capacity.

The broader tailwind is that refineries are operating at high utilization rates with tight fuel inventories (gasoline and diesel supplies remain lean), allowing them to profit from the spread between crude costs and refined product prices even as oil prices pull back. This combination—lower input costs meeting strong refining demand—has supported the sector's gains over the past two weeks.
